description: BRATIXLAB is a technology and innovation team focused on software development, AI, blockchain, and emerging technologies. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to develop practical solutions for astronaut health monitoring. We welcome passionate developers, AI and data science enthusiasts, UI/UX designers, researchers, biomedical experts, and problem-solvers. We value creativity, teamwork, commitment, and a willingness to learn. Join us to turn ideas into impact!
summary: VytaCare is a health self-assessment and decision-support app for astronauts on long-duration missions. Astronauts log a daily check-in covering blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, oxygen saturation, blood glucose, sleep, mood, stress, exercise, cabin air and symptoms. Instead of fixed thresholds, VytaCare compares each reading with the astronaut's own baseline and configured limits, and a trend model spots slow drift before a limit is crossed. Every alert explains what changed, why it fired and what to do next, and says when to contact the flight surgeon. An interactive body map shows how spaceflight affects the heart, lungs, brain, eyes, metabolism, bones and immune system, while a daily routine with streaks keeps healthy habits on track. Astronauts, Medical Officers and Mission Administrators each get their own dashboard, and the app keeps working offline and syncs when the link returns. All 17 NASA Human Research Program risks are mapped to features. As missions go to the Moon and Mars, ground support will be delayed, so crews must catch health changes early. VytaCare is a research prototype on simulated data. It supports decisions and does not diagnose.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

VytaCare helps astronauts assess their own health when help from Earth is slow or far away. Each day the astronaut logs a check-in: blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, oxygen saturation, blood glucose, sleep, mood, stress, exercise, cabin CO2, radiation dose and symptoms. The first seven days set the astronaut's personal baseline. Engine A checks every reading against configured limits and against that baseline, and flags combined patterns such as heart rate up, oxygen down and CO2 high. Engine B is a trend model that spots slow drift over several days before any limit is crossed. Findings are merged into one per topic, and each one explains what changed, since when, why it fired, what to do next and which NASA risk it relates to. Emergency symptoms such as chest pain raise an immediate "contact the flight surgeon" alert. An interactive body map explains how spaceflight affects seven body systems. A daily routine with streaks and badges keeps healthy habits on track. The astronaut, the Medical Officer and the Mission Administrator each get their own dashboard. The app is offline-first: readings and alerts are saved on the device and sync to the server when the link returns.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Crews catch health changes earlier, understand them, and know when to escalate, even when ground replies take a long time. Medical Officers see the whole crew in one place. Administrators see status only, so sensitive data stays protected. We want crews on Moon and Mars missions to act with more confidence and less dependence on real-time ground support. The same approach could later help remote and isolated settings on Earth.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, IndexedDB.

Backend: Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, JWT sessions, scrypt password hashing, audit log.

Quality and delivery: pytest, Docker, Git and GitHub.

Data: simulated astronaut data for three crew scenarios (nominal, isolation drift, cabin air). No hardware was used. Wearable and camera input are planned.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Instead of one threshold for everyone, VytaCare learns each astronaut's own normal. Its alerts always explain themselves. It is aware of the mission environment (space station, deep-space transit, Moon base, Mars surface) and changes its guidance when ground replies are slow. Three separate role dashboards, a clickable body map and gamified daily health habits make a clinical tool approachable for non-clinicians.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Scientific honesty: VytaCare supports decisions and never claims to diagnose, and its limits are examples that a flight surgeon would set. Distance and delay: offline operation and autonomy guidance. Privacy: role-based access, hashed passwords, audit logging. Explainability: no unexplained "high risk" labels. Usability: plain instructions for people who are not medical experts, and status shown with words as well as color. Scope: all 17 NASA Human Research Program risks are mapped to features, with 4 fully automated, 7 tracked with trends and 6 as structured logs.
